title: fip-mcp Gateway Service: Core Infrastructure & KB Tools
description: The FORGE KB MCP Server is a unified gateway for all Bedrock Knowledge Base operations across FIP apps. It exposes KB search, ingest, and metadata as standard MCP tools over HTTP/SSE — so FAIT v2 Claude Code agents (and any other FIP service) can call a single, authenticated endpoint instead of wiring bedrock-agent-runtime directly into each app.

title: As a client application, I want Entra OAuth authentication validation so that only authorized FIP users can access KB tools
description:
## Developer Brief — Entra OAuth authentication validation
**Spec Reference:** Section 4
### Context
All MCP requests must be authenticated via Entra OAuth bearer tokens. The server validates JWT signatures, claims, and tenant membership before allowing access to KB operations.
### Scope
Includes: JWT validation middleware, Entra JWKS integration, token claim extraction (oid, groups, roles, tid), auth error responses. Does NOT include: entitlement checking (that's per-tool), admin role validation (separate story).
### Technical Notes
Use jsonwebtoken + jwks-rsa for validation. Extract oid, groups, roles, tid claims for downstream use. Return 401 for missing/invalid tokens, before any tool logic runs.
### Dependencies
Entra client configuration (ENTRA_CLIENT_ID, ENTRA_TENANT_ID) must be available in environment.
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid Entra JWT with correct aud and tid, when making MCP request, then authentication succeeds
Given missing Authorization header, when making MCP request, then 401 Unauthorized is returned
Given expired JWT token, when making MCP request, then 401 Unauthorized is returned
Given valid token with wrong tenant, when making MCP request, then 401 Unauthorized is returned
Given valid token, when processing request, then oid, groups, and roles claims are extracted

parentTitle: Implement KB Entitlement System with Fallback Configuration
title: As the system, I want entitlement service with DB and fallback support so that KB access can be controlled properly
description:
## Developer Brief — Entitlement service with DB and fallback support
**Spec Reference:** Section 3
### Context
KB access control uses a two-tier system: database-driven entitlements (primary) when FAIT v2 DB exists, and static configuration (fallback) before the DB is available. This service determines read/write access for each user/KB combination.
### Scope
Includes: entitlement lookup service, database connection handling, fallback config loading, group-based entitlement resolution. Does NOT include: tool implementations, auto-scoping logic, or admin endpoints.
### Technical Notes
Priority order: DB lookup first, then fallback config. Fallback uses Entra groups + defaults. NEXUS KB is always readable for authenticated users. Cache entitlement results per request to avoid repeated lookups.
### Dependencies
FAIT v2 DB connection string (when available), fallback entitlements config file, Entra group claims from auth middleware.
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Given user_id and kb_id, when checking entitlements, then correct read/write flags are returned
Given database is available, when looking up entitlements, then DB table is queried first
Given database is unavailable, when looking up entitlements, then fallback config is used
Given user in Entra groups, when using fallback, then group permissions are merged with defaults
Given NEXUS KB access, when checking any authenticated user, then read access is always granted

title: As a FAIT agent, I want search_kb MCP tool with auto-scoping so that I can retrieve KB content securely
description:
## Developer Brief — search_kb MCP tool with auto-scoping
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.1
### Context
The search_kb tool is the primary KB retrieval mechanism. It must automatically inject security filters based on KB type and user identity, then call Bedrock Agent Runtime Retrieve API.
### Scope
Includes: search_kb tool handler, auto-scoping filter injection by KB type, Bedrock API integration, entitlement validation, error handling. Does NOT include: entitlement service (separate), other tools, or admin features.
### Technical Notes
Follow FIP patterns for MCP tool implementation. Auto-inject filters per Section 3.1 table — Personal KB gets user_id filter, Team KB requires team_id validation, etc. Merge caller filters with security filters using AND logic.
### Dependencies
Entitlement service, Bedrock IAM permissions, KB inventory configuration.
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid KB ID and read entitlement, when calling search_kb, then relevant chunks are returned
Given Personal KB access, when searching, then user_id filter is auto-injected from token.oid
Given Team KB access, when searching with team_id, then team membership is validated
Given caller-provided filters, when security filters exist, then both are merged with AND logic
Given invalid KB ID, when calling search_kb, then 400 UNKNOWN_KB error is returned
Given no read entitlement, when calling search_kb, then 403 NOT_ENTITLED error is returned

**Spec Reference:** Section 3.2
### Context
Clients need to discover which KBs the authenticated user can access. This tool returns the filtered list based on entitlements, with NEXUS KB always included for authenticated users.

### Dependencies
Entitlement service, KB inventory configuration.
### Open Questions
None

parentTitle: Implement Core KB MCP Tools
title: As a content creator, I want add_to_kb MCP tool so that I can ingest content into KBs asynchronously
description:
## Developer Brief — add_to_kb MCP tool
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.3
### Context
The add_to_kb tool enables content ingestion into KBs. It validates write permissions, required metadata fields, and triggers async ingestion via Bedrock, returning immediately with a job ID for polling.
### Scope
Includes: add_to_kb tool handler, write entitlement validation, metadata validation, Bedrock ingestion trigger, job ID generation. Does NOT include: synchronous ingestion, job polling (separate tool), or content preprocessing.
### Technical Notes
Validate write entitlement first. Require source and created_by in metadata. Call bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob or S3-based trigger (Tony to determine). Return job_id immediately for get_job_status polling.
### Dependencies
Entitlement service, Bedrock IAM permissions, job tracking system (in-memory for MVP).
### Open Questions
S3 trigger vs direct StartIngestionJob API — Tony to verify against KB data source configuration
acceptanceCriteria: Given write entitlement, when calling add_to_kb with valid content and metadata, then job_id is returned
Given missing write entitlement, when calling add_to_kb, then 403 WRITE_NOT_ENTITLED is returned
Given missing source or created_by metadata, when calling add_to_kb, then 400 METADATA_REQUIRED is returned
Given Project KB, when metadata lacks project_id, then 400 PROJECT_ID_REQUIRED is returned

description:
## Developer Brief — get_kb_metadata MCP tool
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.4
### Context
Clients need access to KB metadata like document count, last update time, and configuration details. This tool provides that information via Bedrock APIs.

Includes: get_kb_metadata tool handler, read entitlement validation, Bedrock API integration for KB info and ingestion jobs. Does NOT include: write operations, content retrieval, or admin features.

### Dependencies
Entitlement service, Bedrock IAM permissions, KB inventory configuration.
### Open Questions
None

parentTitle: Implement Core KB MCP Tools
title: As a client application, I want get_job_status MCP tool so that I can poll async operation progress
description:
## Developer Brief — get_job_status MCP tool
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.5
### Context
This is the universal async polling tool for all FIP MCP operations. It tracks job status across different operation types, starting with KB ingestion jobs but designed to handle future async tools.
### Scope
Includes: get_job_status tool handler, job routing by type, Bedrock GetIngestionJob integration, job result formatting. Does NOT include: job creation (that's in other tools), synchronous operations, or job cancellation.
### Technical Notes
For KB ingestion jobs, call bedrock-agent-runtime:GetIngestionJob. For MVP, in-memory job tracking is sufficient. Design the job routing to handle future job types (not just KB jobs).
### Dependencies
Job tracking system, Bedrock IAM permissions.
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Given valid job_id for KB ingestion, when calling get_job_status, then current status is returned
Given completed job, when checking status, then result object is included in response
Given failed job, when checking status, then error message is included
Given invalid job_id, when calling get_job_status, then appropriate error is returned

title: As FIRM transcriber, I want to migrate from bedrock-agent-runtime to add_to_kb so that KB ingestion is centralized
description:
## [Task Name]
**Before:** FIRM's firm-transcriber Batch container calls bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob directly to push meeting summaries to Personal KB (ZCEZCJGHQC)
**After:** firm-transcriber calls fip-mcp add_to_kb MCP tool with Entra authentication for the same functionality
**Migration Steps:**
1. Update firm-transcriber to authenticate with Entra OAuth for fip-mcp calls
2. Replace bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob calls with HTTP POST to fip-mcp add_to_kb tool
3. Update job polling logic to use fip-mcp get_job_status instead of direct GetIngestionJob calls
4. Remove bedrock-agent-runtime SDK dependencies from firm-transcriber
5. Update IAM role to remove Bedrock permissions (now handled by fip-mcp)
**Validation:** Meeting summary ingestion continues to work with same content reaching Personal KB
**Rollback:** Revert to direct Bedrock calls by restoring previous firm-transcriber version and IAM permissions
